slotContracts.result: r0 = 0 after T is reset dormant (0x43dd0) and T+0x30 = 1. Before the reset, under the record lock: state bit0 (ready or running) unlinks T through 0x43d20; state bit1 without bit5 calls 0x446fc (cancels the timer when [T+0x14] is nonzero, unlinks from the object queue when state bit4) without the object's lock; state bit1 with bit5 (state 0x32) takes the cross-object path; other nonzero states (for example 4) need no unlink. After the reset a queued activation (T+0xe bit0) is cleared and T restarted through 0x43f70. If the unlink or restart returned nonzero, 0x44018(record+0) runs: local -> 0x43640(-12) dispatch with context save after the unlock; remote -> interrupt 120 at core record+0 >> 1. Cross-object path: T+0x24 = 1, release lock_a, take the lock of g_contexts[[T+0x14]+0x8 - 1] (record2+0x14), retake lock_a (IRQ stays masked throughout); if T+0x24 was cleared meanwhile (a releaser terminated T) it unlocks both and returns 0 with CPSR.I clear; else 0x446fc, release the object lock, reset as above. A state-0x32 target that already has T+0x24 set (another core's termination is between its two lock phases) returns at once: 0 after clearing a queued activation (T+0xe bit0), else -41, T stays waiting, and this path returns with CPSR.I still set.

Sets CPSR.I and takes the selected class record's object lock (dom+0x14 via [dom+0x18], release [dom+0x1c]). When the receiver (rec+0xc) list is nonempty, the body takes the first receiver (rec+0xc)'s domain scheduler lock (dom' = A 0x400545cc / B 0x400e458c + (T+0x20 - 1)*132, +0x8 via [dom'+0xc], release [dom'+0x10]), unlinks T, stores [T+0x14]+0xc := r1, and A 0x44568 / B 0xd4528 (dom', T) readies it. When that returns 0 the body drops both locks and returns 0 without dispatch or notification. Otherwise A 0x44018 / B 0xd3fd4 runs on dom'+0x0 (A local for 0/1, B local for 0/2): a return of 1 makes the body call dispatcher A 0x43640 / B 0xd3640 after dropping both locks, and 0 means the peer notification (interrupt 120) was raised. When the ring is full: wait-info+0xc := r1, then the body takes the executing domain's scheduler lock (*(A 0x400545c8 / B 0x400e4588)+0x8 via +0xc, release +0x10). It requires the current T state byte +0xc bit0; when clear it drops both locks, clears CPSR.I and restarts from the object lock (unbounded spin). This is the only live restart. Then A 0x44800 / B 0xd47c0 queues T on rec+0x0 and the call dispatches with context save. Every path after the lock clears CPSR.I on exit. Lock acquires (object lock record +0x14 via [+0x18], scheduler lock record +0x8 via [+0xc]) call A 0x439d8 / B 0xd398c, installed for both class records by A 0x43ac0 / B 0xd3a7c, which spins with ldrex/strex until the word is taken, issues a DMB and returns 0; the spin runs with CPSR.I set and a held lock only lengthens it. slotContracts.arguments: class = r0 asr 16; class 1 or 2 selects the inline class record A 0x400545cc / B 0x400e458c + (class-1)*132; class 0 selects the executing domain's record via A 0x400545c8 / B 0x400e4588; any other class is -18. n = sxth(r0); n <= 0 or n > class record +0x60 (120) is -18; rec = [class record +0x5c] + (n-1)*32. r1: pointer receiving one word, not validated. r2 = timeout in kernel clock units (deadline = executing domain clock word + r2, 10 per tick); -1 waits without a timer, 0 polls, positive arms a timer, below -1 is -17.
slotContracts.result: r0 = 0 with *r1 = a word when one is available. With a waiting sender and a nonempty ring: *r1 = oldest buffered word (0x48fa4) and the sender's word ([T+0x14]+0xc) is appended by 0x48edc. With a waiting sender and an empty ring: *r1 = the sender's word. Either way the sender is unlinked and readied by 0x44568. Without a sender and a nonempty ring: *r1 = the oldest word. Empty with r2 = 0: r0 = -50. Empty otherwise: the task blocks and r0 = wait-info+0 on resumption; only 0 also writes *r1 = wait-info+0xc.

slotContracts.context: Requires context word 0, CPSR.I clear and dispatch-enabled word nonzero at entry, else -25. Sets CPSR.I and takes the class record object lock (+0x14 via [+0x18], release [+0x1c]). When the sender (rec+0x0) list is nonempty, the body takes the first sender (rec+0x0)'s domain scheduler lock (dom' = A 0x400545cc / B 0x400e458c + (T+0x20 - 1)*132, +0x8 via [dom'+0xc], release [dom'+0x10]), unlinks T, moves the word as the result describes, and A 0x44568 / B 0xd4528 (dom', T) readies it. When that returns 0 the body drops both locks and returns 0 without dispatch or notification. (A 0x4a99c-0x4a9b8). Otherwise A 0x44018 / B 0xd3fd4 runs on dom'+0x0 (A local for 0/1, B local for 0/2): a return of 1 makes the body call dispatcher A 0x43640 / B 0xd3640 after dropping both locks, and 0 means the peer notification (interrupt 120) was raised. To block (empty ring, r2 != 0) the body takes the executing domain's scheduler lock (*A 0x400545c8 / B 0x400e4588 +0x8 via +0xc, release +0x10). It requires the current T state byte +0xc bit0; when clear it drops both locks, clears CPSR.I and restarts from the object lock (unbounded spin). This is the only live restart. It then sets T+0xc := 18 and calls A 0x444e4 / B 0xd44a4 (wait-info, timer node, r2), which removes T from the ready queue, sets T+0x14 := wait-info, and arms the timer node (callback A 0x44318 / B 0xd42d8, node+8 = T) only for r2 > 0, else writes wait-info+0 := 0. A positive r2 is added to the executing domain's clock [[*(A 0x400545c8 / B 0x400e4588)+0x40]], not the class-selected record's. T is linked at the tail of the receiver list (rec+0xc/+0x10) regardless of the attribute. Wait-info +0x4 := rec. Wait-info +0x8 := the class value, or 1 (A) / 2 (B) for class 0. The body drops both locks and calls A 0x43640 / B 0xd3640. Every path that took the object lock clears CPSR.I on exit. Census: every A and B call entered with IRQ unmasked, context word 0 and r2 = -1. Lock acquires (object lock record +0x14 via [+0x18], scheduler lock record +0x8 via [+0xc]) call A 0x439d8 / B 0xd398c, installed for both class records by A 0x43ac0 / B 0xd3a7c, which spins with ldrex/strex until the word is taken, issues a DMB and returns 0; the spin runs with CPSR.I set and a held lock only lengthens it. Release A 0x43a14 / B 0xd39c8 is DMB, store 0, DSB.

preconditions.name: destructor-id-overrun
preconditions.statement: Destructor 0x724f08(n) passes its message queue's encoded data-queue/pool id (class<<16)|n to +0xd0 of the executing core's root where data-queue delete +0xa4 belongs, so data queue n stays created. For n >= 2 the body writes {2, 32, 0} over the per-task eventflag creation record of task n-1 (A 0x4005d178 + (n-2)*12 / B 0x400ed138 + (n-2)*12); its cleared exists word makes later flag set/wait/clear/poll on task n-1 return -42. It also writes a self-link at +0x0/+0x4 and 0 at +0xc of A 0x40062c34 + (n-1)*20 / B 0x400f2bf4 + (n-1)*20, below the boot stack top A 0x40063460 / B 0x400f3420 (loader-40000.dis:13691-13718). Observed on the stock POWER OFF route: n = 8 and n = 41 on core 0 in domain A; task 7 and task 40 records changed from {4, 0, 1} to {2, 0x20, 0}.

slotContracts.context: Task context only: context word (A 0x400545a4 / B 0x400e4564) 0, CPSR.I clear and dispatch-enabled word (A 0x40054764 / B 0x400e4724) nonzero, all checked before any state change. The acquire installed in every record (A 0x439d8 / B 0xd398c) spins on ldrex/strexeq until it holds the word and always returns 0, so the body's failed-acquire branches are unreachable and contention spins inside the acquire with CPSR.I set. If the pool is exhausted it also takes the executing domain's scheduler lock (*A 0x400545c8 / B 0x400e4588 +0x8 via +0xc, release +0x10). If current T state bit0 (byte T+0xc, current T word A 0x40054760 / B 0x400e4720) is clear with both locks held, it releases both, unmasks IRQ and loops without bound; this is the only live retry loop. To wait it calls 0x44800 / 0xd47c0 (T+0xc = 0x32, removes T from its ready queue via 0x43d20 / 0xd3cdc, T+0x14 = wait block, wait block +0 = 0, links T by priority T+0xd when creation attribute bit0 is set else at the tail, wait block +4 = CB, +8 = record+4), drops the scheduler and object locks, and dispatches through 0x43640 / 0xd3640 with IRQ masked (the -73 loaded into r0 is overwritten). Exits with IRQ unmasked.

slotContracts.domainNotes: Slot bodies are byte-identical (same sha256); the decomp names them kernel_core_index_adapter (kernel0 core/entry_adapters.c) and xm1_kernel1_core_index_entry (kernel1 core/secondary_entry_adapters.c). slotContracts.arguments: r0: pointer to a lock word, or 0 for the default word 0x400c0804. r1: value stored on acquisition, not checked. Stock image4 callers pass r0 = 0 (0x7235d8) or 0x409c2808 + 4*i for i 0..4 (0x725940), and r1 = (core index + 1) | 0x20.
slotContracts.result: r0 = 0 after an exclusive store of r1 into a word that read 0, followed by a DMB (mcr p15, 0, rX, c7, c10, 5). r0 = -1 at once when the word reads nonzero. A failed strex retries the exclusive load; a held word is never waited on. Called from an IRQ handler with r0 = 0 it always returns -1, because the stock IRQ vector holds 0x400c0804 (tag 17 or 18) for the whole handler.

errors.meaning: lock word nonzero

slotContracts.context: Any context and mode; no IRQ masking, context-word or core check; never blocks. The default word 0x400c0804 is the same physical address in A and B and is also the stock IRQ vector's cross-core lock: the vector body A 0x40258-0x402bc / B 0xd0258-0xd02bc (literal 0x4041c / 0xd041c) acquires it through A 0x427d4 / B 0xd27d4 with tag 17 (core index 0) or 18 (core index 1), passes when the word already holds its own tag, spins with CPSR.I set on any other nonzero value, and releases it at A 0x4030c / B 0xd030c when the context-word nesting count returns to 0. 17 and 18 equal (core index + 1) | 0x10, the value wrapper 0x7235d8 treats as already owned. [INFERENCE] ldrex/strex on this word serialises the two cores; the cross-core exclusive-monitor behaviour is unverified (law U12, reports/xm1-timer-interrupt-laws.md).
objects: lock word, default 0x400c0804, shared by A, B and the stock IRQ vector of both cores (tags 17/18 from the vector, (core index + 1) | 0x20 from image4 wrappers)

preconditions.name: aligned-lock-word
preconditions.statement: A nonzero r0 points to a word-aligned word in memory that supports ldrex/strex.

preconditions.name: nonzero-lock-value
preconditions.statement: r1 is nonzero; storing 0 returns 0 but leaves the word reading free.

preconditions.name: holder-masks-irq
preconditions.statement: A task-context holder of 0x400c0804 keeps CPSR.I set on its own core from acquire to release. An IRQ taken on the holding core spins forever at A 0x40258 / B 0xd0258 with IRQ masked, and while the word is held every IRQ entry on both cores waits. Stock wrapper 0x7235d8 masks through +0x164 before acquiring.

slotContracts.domainNotes: Slot bodies are byte-identical (same sha256) and both load the literal 0x400c0804. The callee is each kernel's own copy (A 0x427d4 / B 0xd27d4), instruction-identical apart from the branch target.

slotContracts.arguments: r0: pointer to a lock word, or 0 for the default word 0x400c0804.
slotContracts.result: r0 = 0 after an exclusive store of 0 into a word that read nonzero, followed by a DMB. r0 = -1 when the word already reads 0. Any nonzero value is cleared: there is no owner check. The DMB follows the releasing store; no barrier precedes it. Called from an IRQ handler with r0 = 0 it clears the IRQ vector's hold (tag 17 or 18) on 0x400c0804 and returns 0.
